If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me not to make my 7-year-old brother go to sleep when he stayed up late watching a movie with my friend. Let me break this down step by step. First, I know that my brother is pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he doesn't get enough sleep, he gets all out of sorts the next day. That makes sense because kids his age need a lot of sleep to grow and function properly. So, in an ideal world, he should be in bed by a certain time to ensure he gets enough rest. Last night, my mom left me in charge and trusted me to handle things while she was out. She even said it was fine if I had my one friend over. I made sure my brother went to bed on time, and he can usually put himself to bed, so I thought everything was under control. Then my friend came over, and we started goofing around, watching a movie, and being kind of loud. That's when my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, and I said no, telling him to go back to bed. But my friend said we should let him stay. I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now, I would basically have to drag him upstairs, which would lead to a fit and be embarrassing and exhausting. So, I let him sit on the couch with us. By the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home, my brother was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs and put him in bed. It was like midnight. The next morning, he didn't want to get up, even though on weekends he's not allowed to sleep past like 8. He was pretty cranky. My mom found out I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7, he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later, he won't feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her that two hours of missed sleep for a kid his age wasn't a big deal. So, the question is: Was it right or wrong for me not to force him to go to bed? I need to figure out if my actions were appropriate or not. First, I need to consider the importance of sleep for a 7-year-old. According to experts, children that age typically need about 10-12 hours of sleep per night. If he stayed up until midnight instead of his usual bedtime, that's a significant loss of sleep. Two hours might not seem like a lot to me, but for a child, it can have noticeable effects. Next, I should think about the immediate consequences. The next day, he was cranky and didn't want to get up. That's a clear sign that he didn't get enough sleep. It's not just about the quantity of sleep but also the quality. If he was woken up by us being loud, he might not have gotten the restful sleep he needed. Then there's the aspect of setting boundaries and teaching responsibility. If I let him stay up late this time, does that set a precedent for future behavior? He might think it's okay to stay up late whenever he wants, especially if he knows he can get his way by being persistent or throwing a fit. On the other hand, I was in a tough spot. My friend was over, and I didn't want to cause a scene by dragging him upstairs. Plus, he was already half-asleep by the end of the movie, so carrying him up wasn't too bad. Maybe in that moment, it seemed like the lesser of two evils. I also need to consider my mom's perspective. She trusted me to handle things, and when she found out, she got mad. That means she probably thinks it's important to stick to the routine, especially since she knows how sensitive he is to missed sleep. Another thing to think about is the long-term effects. If this happens occasionally, it might not be a big deal, but if it becomes a regular occurrence, it could lead to chronic sleep deprivation, which has more serious consequences like behavioral issues, difficulty concentrating, and overall poor health. I also wonder about the role of empathy here. My brother was excited to watch the movie with us, and it's natural for a kid his age to want to be included in what the older kids are doing. By letting him stay, I was being considerate of his feelings, but I also had to balance that with his well-being. There's also the aspect of peer influence. My friend, who doesn't have a little sibling, thinks my brother is cute and hyped him up. That might have contributed to my brother being more riled up and less likely to go back to bed. So, it's not just my decision but also influenced by external factors. In the end, I need to weigh the immediate consequences against the long-term implications. While letting him stay up late once might not have severe effects, it's about establishing a consistent routine and teaching him about responsibility and consequences. I also need to think about how to handle similar situations in the future. Maybe setting clear expectations beforehand, like explaining that if he stays up late, he might feel tired the next day, and encouraging him to go to bed on time. That way, he understands the connection between his actions and the outcomes. Additionally, communication with my mom is important. Explaining my reasoning and understanding her concerns can help bridge the gap and ensure that we're on the same page regarding his sleep routine. So, after considering all these factors, I need to decide whether not making him go to bed was the right or wrong decision.
